claim: In the third environment-assisted weak-measurement-reversal scheme of Xu, Cheng, Liu, Su, Wang, and Zhang for two equally amplitude-damped qubits, let \(d\in(0,1)\) be the damping strength and \(q\in[0,1]\) the reversal strength. With \(r=1-d\) and \(y=1-q\), their displayed formulas imply \[C_3(q)=\frac{2r\sqrt y}{r+y},\qquad P_3(q)=\frac{r+y}{2}.\]The concurrence is uniquely maximized at \(y=r\), hence at \(q=d\), with \[C_{3,\max}=\sqrt{1-d},\qquad P_3(q=d)=1-d.\]The paper instead labels \(q_{\mathrm{pub}}=2d-d^2\) as optimal; this has \(y=r^2\) and gives \[C_{\mathrm{pub}}=\frac{2r}{1+r},\qquad P_{\mathrm{pub}}=\frac{r(1+r)}2.\]For every \(0<d<1\), the corrected point strictly dominates the published point in both quantities: \[C_{3,\max}-C_{\mathrm{pub}}=\frac{\sqrt r(1-\sqrt r)^2}{1+r}>0,\qquad P_3(q=d)-P_{\mathrm{pub}}=\frac{r(1-r)}2>0.\]Moreover, the complete concurrence-success Pareto frontier of this one-parameter scheme is \(0\le q\le d\), equivalently \(r\le P\le(1+r)/2\), with \[C_{\mathrm{Pareto}}(P)=\frac{r\sqrt{2P-r}}{P}.\]Thus the source's stated scheme-three optimum lies on the strictly dominated branch \(q>d\); comparisons in that paper that substitute the published scheme-three optimum require recomputation. No claim is made about the other two schemes or about globally optimal entanglement-restoration protocols.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; the packaged checker provides supplementary finite replay
integrity.novelty_scope: Correction of the scheme-three scalar optimization, strict two-coordinate domination of the published point, and the complete concurrence-success Pareto frontier for that source model.
integrity.source_date_basis: The exact archive anchor is the author-uploaded public full text dated 2015-10-07; later journal dates are not used as the first-public-date field.

scientific_limitations: The correction applies only to the third scheme with equal amplitude damping and the source's one-parameter reverse weak measurement.
It does not establish global optimality over all environment-assisted or weak-measurement protocols.
Only later comparisons that substitute the source's stated scheme-three optimum are asserted to require recomputation; no universal ranking of all schemes is claimed.
An equivalent correction may exist in unindexed literature or under a different reversal-strength convention.
title: Correcting the optimal reversal strength in an environment-assisted entanglement-restoration scheme
